text:
maria: FYI we're seeing % validation rejects for fncall.tool-invoke in ap-south during the private canary after enabling strict validation mode. pattern is different from earlier: tools sometimes return null for optional fields, and validator bubbles as hard rejects. anyone on-call?

alex: I can jump in. quick thought: instead of full rollback, can we flip a validator mode to `soft-coerce` that attempts to fix shapes and emits `validation.warning` telemetry? That would keep customers online.

ravi: technically doable. proto: validator returns `result` + `validation.provenance` array that lists coerced paths. sample response: 
```
{
  "result": {"items": [{"id":"x","value":[]} ]},
  "validation": {"mode":"soft-coerce","warnings":["response.items[0].value coerced array->object"],"provenance":["response.items[0].value"]}
}
```

sara: console/UX ask: any auto-coercion must be visible in the route dashboard and in request inspector with an easy way to filter by `validation.warnings`. we also need threshold banners when warnings > 0.5% for 15m.

console-team: agreed. propose adding a small colored chip next to route name showing `soft-coerce` rate, and a collapsible inspector section that shows diffs (before/after) for the sanitized payload.

ops-bot: Alert: validation.reject rate > 0.4% on route fncall.tool-invoke (ap-south)  ticket #INC-7902 opened.

alex: billing question: do we mark coerced responses as unbillable, partially-billed, or normal? finance input needed.

finance: short answer: customers shouldn't be billed for platform-caused regressions. marking everything unbillable is risky for abuse. prefer marking coercions as `billing_adj=true` and flagging invoices with an adjustment line while we triage. Also want a daily report.

ravi: proposed rollout plan: 
1) enable `soft-coerce` as a per-route feature flag (canary slice=5%)
2) add routeOverride to route table: 
```
- route: fncall.tool-invoke
  when: validation.rejects.rate > 0.003
  action: enable_validator_mode
  mode: soft-coerce
  telemetryTags: ["validation_softcoerce","canary:5pct"]
  billingTag: billing_adj
```
3) sample full payloads to secure bucket `s3://redwood-debug/aps/1822502468/` with 72h retention

sara: UX + console: provide an explainer link in the banner that opens a lite doc describing `soft-coerce` semantics and billing implications. also add a CTA to toggle route back to strict.

alex: ops runbook change: if `validation.reject.rate` drops < 0.1% after soft-coerce, we keep mode enabled for 24h and notify adapters teams to patch. if rejects stay > 1% escalate to rollback.

maria: I'm +1 on incremental approach. two asks before flip: a) telemetry must include `validation.mode` and `coercion_count` b) add a sampling policy for logs so we don't leak PII.

ravi: will include tags: `validation.mode`, `coercion_count`, `route_variant`. sampling config will redact PII and keep 200 example payloads per hour.

ops-bot: Update: validator featureflag `soft-coerce` toggled ON for fncall.tool-invoke canary at 03:15 UTC. Reject rate dropped ~70% in first 12m.

console-team: started a draft mock for the route banner + inspector diff. sharing in #design later today.

finance: opened billing_adj workflow ticket #BILL-154 with template for invoice adjustments and daily report CSV.

alex: follow-ups: 1) retro doc with adapter test-cases (array/null/object permutations) 2) QA harness to inject malformed responses in CI 3) decision by EOD on whether `soft-coerce` becomes GA or remains a temporary mitigant.

maria: thanks. holding main rollout until we have adapter fixes or a billing policy. will update in 45m. :thumbsup:
